messages:
rachel: Heads-up: noticed sporadic chart stalls on first load after yesterday's client release. small sparkline and table charts pause ~250-600ms.
omar: saw that too. flamegraph shows a large synchronous eval inside chart splitpoint; looks like a new dependency got tangled into the chart chunk.
vik: checking bundle map now. yep — `formatting-core` and `timezones` ended up in the charts splitpoint because of a transitive import from `chart-utils`.
perf-bot: alert: LCP 90th percentile increased by ~320ms for canary users at 05:10 UTC.
rachel: I think this was introduced by the splitpoint refactor PR that tried to consolidate chart code; the manual split annotations might have been overwritten by the bundler rename.
omar: quick mitigation options: 1) hotfix to add explicit dynamic imports for `timezones` and `formatting-core` 2) reduce prefetch parallelism to avoid thundering parses 3) pause canary rollout.
vik: minimal hotfix snippet:
```js
// force separate chunk for heavy deps
const tz = () => import(/* webpackChunkName: "tz" */ 'timezones')
const fmt = () => import(/* webpackChunkName: "fmt" */ 'formatting-core')
```
Then ensure chart widgets only call tz()/fmt() after firstPaint.
qa: also seeing backend 429s correlated with these stalls; router prefetch retries when hydration hangs and that floods the data API. lowering client prefetch concurrency will reduce pressure.
deploy-bot: canary scale change requested by rachel: set to 0%.
vik: i'm opening hotfix PR now. will include deferred init and a small throttle on parallel widget hydration.
omar: follow-ups: add CI assertion that validates splitpoint contents (no locales/timezone libs in chart chunk) and a perf smoke that loads 3 dashboards in parallel.
rachel: agreed. also schedule a quick postmortem doc so we record why the manual split got lost and propose a lint rule for explicit chunk annotations.
vik: will include that in the PR description. merging hotfix once CI green, then we can re-enable canary at 5% and monitor.
perf-bot: staging perf run queued by QA; will post results in ~8m.
qa: staging results look good: parse time reduced ~280ms, LCP back to baseline, backend 429s dropped ~70%.
rachel: closing loop. thanks all. we'll still follow up with the RFC on splitpoint ownership and a CI guard. :thumbsup:
